title: Cavity-enhanced superconducting response in an underdoped cuprate
authors: Angela Montanaro, Vadim Plastovets, Nitesh Khatiwada, Jacopo Fiore, Giacomo Jarc, Abdullah Alabbadi, Antonio Mastropasqua, Enrico Maria Rigoni, Shahla Y. Mathengattil, Simone Dal Zilio, Francesca Fassioli Olsen, Fabio Novelli, Stephan Winnerl, Michael A. Sentef, Dante M. Kennes, Andrew J. Millis, Francesco Piazza, Daniele Fausti
abstract: Superconductors carry electrical current without resistance when paired electrons condense into a coherent macroscopic quantum state. In underdoped cuprates, evidence suggests that pairing-related correlations and superconducting fluctuations can survive above the temperature at which global coherence is lost, pointing to phase fluctuations as a key limitation on superconductivity in this regime. Motivated by recent demonstrations of cavity-modified collective states in quantum materials, we investigate whether superconducting coherence can be stabilized by engineering the electromagnetic environment of the superconductor. We study an underdoped YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-δ}$ thin film in a tunable terahertz cavity formed with a semi-transparent gold mirror. From temperature-dependent terahertz transmission measurements, we find that the cavity enhances the superconducting response below the critical temperature, with an increase of the inferred superfluid weight. The effect becomes more pronounced at smaller cavity lengths and is accompanied by an upward shift of the superconducting onset temperature. Calculations based on a cavity-coupled model for phase-fluctuating superconductors capture these trends and support an interpretation in terms of cavity-enhanced phase stiffness. These results showcase the potential of cavity engineering for designing emergent functionalities in correlated systems.
summary: The research demonstrates that confining a superconducting film within an optical cavity enhances its superconducting response in underdoped cuprates. By measuring the change in superfluid weight via THz spectroscopy, the authors confirm that cavity confinement increases the effective phase stiffness of the superconductor. This work showcases cavity engineering as a powerful tool for controlling emergent quantum functionalities in correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates whether engineering the electromagnetic environment using a resonant cavity can enhance superconducting coherence, particularly by stabilizing phase fluctuations in underdoped cuprates.
main_result: Experiments show that placing an underdoped YBCO film inside a terahertz cavity enhances the measured superfluid weight and causes an upward shift in the superconducting onset temperature. Theory confirms this enhancement is due to increased effective phase stiffness ($J$).
method: The research combines THz time-domain spectroscopy measurements with theoretical modeling based on the XY model for phase-fluctuating superconductors.
model_or_system: The physical system is an underdoped YBa2Cu3O7-delta thin film placed inside a tunable Fabry-Pérot terahertz cavity. The theory models superconductivity using the XY Hamiltonian, coupling superconducting phase dynamics to the quantized electromagnetic field of the cavity.
key_observables: Superfluid weight ($ ar{\sigma}_2$), superconducting onset temperature ($T_{onset}$), and the renormalized phase stiffness ($J$).
important_parameters: Cavity length ($L$), temperature ($T$), and the ratio of cavity confinement to intrinsic material parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be described by a phase-only action after integrating out EM fields, and that measurements avoid spurious shifts caused by local heating or misalignment.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature dependence of conductivity ($ ar{\sigma}_2$) confirming enhancement inside the cavity; theoretical plots illustrate how cavity size ($L$) modifies the plasmon dispersion relation and increases the phase stiffness $J$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the problem (phase fluctuations limit cuprate superconductivity) to presenting THz measurements showing cavity enhancement, followed by detailed theoretical derivations using action functionals and Renormalization Group analysis to quantify the resulting increase in phase stiffness.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges condensed matter physics (high-Tc superconductors, phase transitions) with quantum optics/cavity QED principles. The concept of using engineered electromagnetic environments to tune fundamental material parameters like phase stiffness is highly relevant for AMO physicists working on open quantum systems and cavity coupling.
